Jorge / team — following up with a concrete PoC/test plan and a few sample TCO numbers to seed the workbook. See attached MVP test plan (mvp-test-plan.md) and the example cost workbook (fincost-per-1M-tokens.xlsx).

Proposed test matrix (short):
- Cold start latency: 10 sequential single-request cold-starts (measure p50/p95/p99).
- Steady-state throughput: 15-minute runs at target concurrency buckets (50, 100, 200 RPS). Capture throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency and failure rate.
- Batching sweep: run at 50/100/200 RPS with batching window sizes [0ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms] and batch size limits [1, 8, 16].
- Cache scenarios: run same throughput tests with cache hit rates simulated at 0%, 25%, 60% (we can seed a prefix cache using your sample prompts).
- Cost calc: instrument token counts (prompt/completion), request counts, and compute GPU utilization to estimate per-1M token cost. We'll produce a sensitivity table in the workbook.

Sample unit economics (example numbers for discussion only — final numbers come from the PoC telemetry and confirmed pricing):
- Redwood hosted (recommended config): modeled at ~$6.00 per 1M tokens (prompt+completion), assuming 8x batching and 25% cache hit; typical steady-state optimization reduces baseline unit cost by ~20–40% vs cold runs.
- Hyperscaler A (example): modeled at ~$9.50 per 1M tokens for a similar model family, with less control over batching/cache and higher variability in p99 latency under load.
- Hyperscaler B (example): modeled at ~$8.75 per 1M tokens.
- OpenAI-like API (example): modeled at ~$12.00 per 1M tokens for comparable capability.

Key notes on how batching and cache impact TCO:
- Batching increases GPU utilization efficiency; for many workloads we observe 15–35% token-cost reduction moving from single-request to 8–16 request batching depending on model and prompt length.
- Cache (prefix/KV caching) reduces the number of generated tokens on completions and can reduce per-1M token spend substantially if the workload has high repetition — e.g., a 60% cache hit rate can effectively cut generated-completion tokens by 60%, shifting your TCO correspondingly.

What we need from you to run the PoC:
1) A small sample of ~200 representative prompts (you mentioned you'll share those).
2) Confirmation of model family and any required model artifacts or constraints.
3) Non-prod endpoint/auth details (we can provide short-lived API keys and an isolated test environment).

Proposed dates: Thu 3/12 — Mon 3/16 (we can compress to a 3-day window if you prefer).

I'll follow up with the pre-populated workbook and the test scripts. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min alignment call before the run.

Thanks,
